title: One Mobikwik Systems Ltd - 544305 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: MobiKwik posted record Q2 FY27 PAT of INR 11.8 crore and EBITDA of INR 22.7 crore (7.5% margin), its fourth straight profitable quarter.
summary.overview: Total income rose 8% YoY to INR 302 crore and revenue from operations rose 9% YoY to INR 295 crore. Reported EBITDA reached INR 22.7 crore with margin of 7.5%, up 977 bps YoY and 204 bps QoQ, and PAT was INR 11.8 crore, up 55% QoQ. Contribution profit grew about 50% while GMV grew 34-35% YoY in both payments and lending, but consumer UPI GMV was soft QoQ on seasonality and a festive-season shift. Management guided to FY28 PAT of INR 100 crore if UPI MDR is implemented, versus earlier INR 75-80 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Above INR 1,000 crore guided last quarter
Merchant GMV +76% YoY, merchant revenue +150% YoY, +18% QoQ GMV, +29% QoQ revenue
Up 1 bp in quarter as stated

segments.name: Payments (consumer and merchant)
segments.commentary: GMV growth of about 34-35% YoY, but consumer UPI GMV fell QoQ in Q2 on seasonality. Consumer take rate is 16 bps plus; merchant net take rate is about 3-4 bps. Merchant share rising dilutes the consolidated take rate.

segments.name: Lending (digital distribution / FLDG)
segments.commentary: Disbursals of INR 1,083 crore in Q2 with 11 active lending partners. 79% of disbursals are under FLDG (5% DLG) and 21% under pure distribution. Processing fees run 3-4% upfront and NIM share accrues over 12-15 months.

guidance_outlook: UPI MDR, once implemented, expected to add at least INR 100 crore to payments revenue in FY28; INR 20-25 crore of that expected to reach EBITDA/PAT.
FY28 PAT target raised to about INR 100 crore if UPI MDR is implemented (earlier target INR 75-80 crore; FY27 target INR 40 crore).
Lending disbursals to keep growing with strong double-digit growth, though not at the same percentage rate.
Management expects better numbers in Q3 FY27 on festive-season spend; fixed costs as % of total income expected to decline in coming quarters.

NBFC plan: aim for about 10% of lending disbursals (about INR 600 crore out of an illustrative INR 6,000 crore) via own NBFC in co-lending 10:90, requiring about INR 60 crore equity; awaiting RBI go-ahead for CoR.
capex_capacity: NBFC: slump sale and migration of credit distribution business completed in August; all RBI conditions met, awaiting final RBI approval for Certificate of Registration before operations start.
Investment in people continuing to support merchant payments and NBFC build-out; employee cost increase described as deliberate build phase, with low base from Q2 FY26 cited.
Fixed costs at about 40% of total income.
demand_pricing: Consumer UPI competition is intense: MobiKwik ranks number 11 among TPAPs; management is shifting to higher-ticket users (transactions above INR 2,000) and deprioritising INR 150-200 ticket transactions.
Merchant side has 2-3 clear competitors per management; merchant net margin cited at 3.4 bps and merchant take rate expected to rise about 2.5 bps after UPI MDR.

UPI MDR: merchant gross take rate 40 bps on eligible transactions above INR 2,000; about 28 bps goes to ecosystem partners; management estimates 8-10 bps net realisable. Consumer side about 8 bps net.
Industry UPI value grew about 1% QoQ in Q2 versus roughly 4% in prior two quarters (NPCI data).
Lending: credit performance improving QoQ, enabling renegotiated partner contracts and better commercials with new partners, lowering lending-related costs as % of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Why did UPI and PPI GMV decline QoQ, and how is consumer UPI growth going to improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited seasonally weak Q2 (industry UPI value +1% QoQ) with festive spend shifting to Q3, and a strategy shift to higher-ticket users above INR 2,000 that may depress near-term numbers; better Q3 expected.

qa_highlights.question: Lending take rate and expense ratios look low; is that due to late-quarter disbursals?
qa_highlights.answer: Soham Roy said disbursals were consistent across the three months; processing fees (3-4%) are upfront while NIM share flows over 12-15 months, so the larger denominator makes ratios look muted. Lending costs fell due to renegotiated partner contracts.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY28 benefit from UPI MDR and how much reaches the bottom line?
qa_highlights.answer: At least INR 100 crore of payments revenue uplift in FY28; roughly 20-25% (INR 20-25 crore) on the merchant side reaches EBITDA/PAT. Cost pass-through to issuing bank, TPAP and PSP is the main offset.

qa_highlights.question: Is lending partner appetite for FLDG versus distribution pushing growth?
qa_highlights.answer: 79% of disbursals are FLDG and 21% pure distribution; management is agnostic and balances both by risk-adjusted returns, staying within the RBI 5% DLG limit.

qa_highlights.question: Will payment take rates stabilise after UPI MDR?
qa_highlights.answer: Soham Roy said take rates were stable QoQ; merchant take rate will improve post-MDR and consumer take rate partially, with a 1-2 bps swing thereafter depending on merchant mix. Consolidated uplift will be smaller than the 2.5 bps peer example.

qa_highlights.question: How long will the employee-cost build phase last and when will fixed cost fall to around 30% of income?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will keep investing in people while it meets growth targets, but said fixed costs as % of total income should decline in upcoming quarters; no specific timeline or 30% target given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the NBFC playbook over 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Asset-light: target about 10% of lending disbursals via own NBFC in co-lending (10:90), needing about INR 60 crore equity for INR 600 crore of disbursal; FLDG stays at 5% guarantee.

risks_watch: UPI MDR timing is still unannounced (originally 15 October, now after Diwali); FY28 upside depends on implementation and final construct.
Competitive intensity expected to rise with MDR; peers may offer free Soundbox devices.
Consumer UPI GMV was soft QoQ; management asked for patience until Q3 numbers.
Fixed costs about 40% of total income; employee costs rising and linked to new business build-out.
RBI approval for the NBFC CoR is pending.
EPS figure in board results (INR 0.75) appeared inconsistent with PAT growth; management said a typo is possible and a correction would be published the next morning.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability and merchant growth, but cautious and somewhat defensive on the soft QoQ consumer UPI GMV, which management attributed to seasonality and a deliberate strategy shift. Management repeatedly declined to quantify MDR economics before final implementation.
key_quotes: This is the fourth consecutive profitable quarter for the company. We have also posted our highest-ever PAT and EBITDA in this quarter.
So we have made a little bit of shift and change in our strategy here. And any time you make certain changes in strategy, there is a short time period when the numbers don't look good.

So in totality, locking in the merchant with a device subscription, generating card-related MDR, wallet-related MDR, RuPay credit card MDR, and then the highly anticipated potential UPI MDR - I think these are all going to be amazing tailwinds for our sector.

adds.what: Own NBFC (co-lending 10:90) for lending disbursals, about INR 600 crore of an illustrative INR 6,000 crore, requires ~INR 60 crore equity; awaiting RBI Certific

growth.why: FY28 PAT target raised to ~INR 100 crore (from INR 75-80 crore) contingent on UPI MDR, which management estimates adds at least INR 100 crore to FY28 payments revenue; revenue grew 9% YoY, with the NBFC licence still pending RBI approval and no firm capacity or order figures behind the revenue growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin hit 7.5% (+977 bps YoY, +204 bps QoQ) and fixed costs at about 40% of total income are expected to decline; UPI MDR could add INR 20-25 crore to EBITDA/PAT in FY28, but MDR timing is unannounced.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Own NBFC slump sale completed in August and all RBI conditions met, but operations start only after RBI grants the Certificate of Registration, which is still pending; lending disbursals of INR 1,083 crore in Q2 run through partners, not owned capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: GMV grew 34-35% YoY in both payments and lending, merchant GMV +76% YoY with +18% QoQ, and management expects better Q3 numbers on festive spend and strong double-digit lending disbursal growth.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management's only capital item is about INR 60 crore of equity for the NBFC, already planned; no utilisation figure is disclosed and no new plant, line or large capex is discussed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY28 PAT target raised to about INR 100 crore from INR 75-80 crore, but only if UPI MDR is implemented; without MDR the earlier range stands and FY27 target is INR 40 crore.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Consumer UPI GMV fell QoQ in Q2 on seasonality and a shift to higher-ticket users, and industry UPI value grew only about 1% QoQ versus roughly 4% in the prior two quarters; MDR delay would remove the FY28 upside.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: NBFC launch (co-lending 10:90, target about 10% of disbursals or INR 600 crore of INR 6,000 crore) is pending RBI CoR; no other product launch was named.

rows.label: UPI MDR implementation
rows.why: MDR at 40 bps gross on transactions above INR 2,000 could add at least INR 100 crore of payments revenue in FY28 and INR 20-25 crore to EBITDA/PAT, but the date was originally 15 October and is still unannounced.

rows.label: RBI Certificate of Registration for NBFC
rows.why: Slump sale completed in August and all RBI conditions met, so only final CoR approval is pending before the NBFC can start operating.

rows.label: Lending partner renegotiation
rows.why: Renegotiated partner contracts have already lowered lending-related costs as a share of revenue, and credit performance is improving QoQ.

tone.note: Management was confident on profitability, merchant growth and the FY28 PAT target, but cautious and somewhat defensive on soft QoQ consumer UPI GMV and declined to quantify MDR economics before final implementation; analysts pushed on the take-rate, lending ratios and fixed-cost trajectory.
